turns.question: What retention outcome should govern uploads that may still be referenced by completed reports?
What should users be told about recovery after deletion, given backups retain objects for 30 days?

contract.G: Automatically clean up old customer uploads under an explicit retention rule that preserves needed report data.
contract.T: Draft a bounded change to delete uploads 90 days after their last report finishes while keeping report summaries, and align user-facing deletion semantics with backup reality.
contract.S: Define retention trigger on last related report completion, preserve report summaries, exclude broader report-data redesign, and cover messaging that deletion is final even though disaster-recovery backups may persist up to 30 days.
contract.V: Contract is satisfied when the retention rule, preserved artifacts, deletion timing, and user-facing recovery semantics are all specified consistently with the repository evidence.
contract.X: Stop if linked uploads are required beyond report summaries, if backup handling must change, or if policy scope expands beyond customer uploads.
contract.P: Persist only through drafting the smallest verifiable retention-policy change; do not implement.

promotions.name: Upload Retention And Deletion Semantics
promotions.evidence: No accepted retention policy exists, uploads may be referenced by completed reports, and backups retain objects for 30 days.

turns.question: What exact privacy boundary should local-only processing enforce for file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI calls, and telemetry?

contract.G: Add local-only file processing with a clear no-egress privacy boundary.
contract.T: Draft a bounded change so file bytes, metadata, and derived text all remain on-device, replacing current remote-AI and telemetry paths as needed for this flow.
contract.S: Cover the primary format supported by the on-device parser, block remote AI use for these files, prevent telemetry from sending file-derived content, and exclude unsupported formats or broader privacy program changes.
contract.V: Contract is satisfied when the local-only boundary explicitly forbids off-device transfer of bytes, metadata, and derived text, including AI and telemetry paths, and fits the current repository evidence.
contract.X: Stop if required functionality depends on unsupported formats, if remote dependencies remain mandatory for the primary flow, or if policy must extend beyond file-processing surfaces.
contract.P: Persist only through the smallest truthful local-only contract slice; do not implement.

promotions.name: Local-Only Processing Boundary
promotions.evidence: A remote AI provider receives derived text today, telemetry can include error payload excerpts, and an on-device parser supports the primary format.

turns.question: What refund authority should support agents have, including any approval threshold and required audit details?
Should support be allowed to issue partial refunds within that authority?

contract.G: Let support agents refund customer payments within a defined authority model.
contract.T: Draft a bounded change granting support authority to issue full or partial refunds up to $100 with a required reason, and require owner approval above that amount.
contract.S: Cover support-role permissions, full and partial refund eligibility within the $100 limit, required reason capture, and creation of an audit event; exclude broader billing-role redesign or payment-provider changes.
contract.V: Contract is satisfied when the authority threshold, approver for larger refunds, partial-refund allowance, and minimum audit requirement are all explicitly specified against the current billing access model.
contract.X: Stop if owner identity or escalation path is undefined, if compliance requires more than reason plus audit event, or if refund scope expands beyond support-initiated payment refunds.
contract.P: Persist only through the smallest verifiable authorization-and-audit contract; do not implement.

promotions.name: Support Refund Authorization And Audit
promotions.evidence: Support currently has read-only billing access, the provider exposes full and partial refund APIs, and no approval threshold or audit event exists.
